- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 14889-14955 (run_standalone_stall_recovery loop body)
  Problem: When GraphQL succeeds but the issue is absent from `_candidate_details_json` (cache miss), the code calls `_staged_support_comments_for_guard` with `cache_available="false"`, which forces a REST fetch. If that REST fetch fails, `comments_json='[]'` and `_standalone_staged_support_comments_unavailable="true"`. The downstream `if [ "${phase}" = "ai:awaiting-approval" ]` block then reads the flag, but the flag is also set unconditionally for every other phase where it is never consulted. The `_standalone_staged_support_latch_release_incomplete` predicate is not run for non-approval phases, so a "released" latch comment that exists in REST (but was not fetched) is irrelevant for them — this is intentional, but the variable name suggests a broader contract.
  Why it fails at runtime: This does not fail at runtime in the new code path; the new test `test_standalone_comment_fetch_failure_only_blocks_approval_recovery` confirms the gated behavior. The minor concern is naming/contract clarity: a future maintainer adding a non-approval latch check might assume the flag is consulted for every phase, when in fact it is only consulted inside the `ai:awaiting-approval` block.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 1

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k3 ===
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 14908-14914 (comment-fetch failure now continues with `comments_json='[]'`), interacting with lines 14996-15017 (state extraction from empty comments resets `status_since_ts` to now), lines 15044-15049 (not-stalled path calls `write_standalone_state_json`), lines 12280/12288 (`_extract_standalone_state_*_from_comments` selects the state marker by `max_by(.created_at // "")`, i.e. newest wins), and lines 12359-12369 (`write_standalone_state_json` with an empty third argument POSTs a brand-new state-marker comment).
  Problem: when the comments REST fetch fails for a non-`ai:awaiting-approval` candidate, the loop now continues with empty comments. With empty comments the extracted standalone state is the default (`status_since_ts:0`), so `updated_state` gets a fresh `status_since_ts = now` and no `stall_recovery_count` / `phase_attempts`; `state_comment_id` is empty, so the not-stalled branch POSTs a NEW `AI_STANDALONE_STALL_STATE_V1` comment every tick. Because extraction later picks the state marker by newest `created_at`, the moment the outage ends these outage-written markers shadow the authoritative pre-outage marker: the stall clock is delayed and `stall_recovery_count` / `phase_attempts` (and `judge_escalate_streak`) are silently reset to 0, re-arming the full `MAX_STALL_RECOVERIES_PER_ISSUE` ladder (and its Telegram alerts / workflow dispatches) for issues that had already consumed their budget. During the outage itself the change cannot do useful work for these phases either — the stall clock lives in the comments, so with comments unavailable no candidate is ever stalled; the only observable effect of "continuing" is the harmful marker write (one extra comment per candidate per 5-minute tick). The new `test_standalone_comment_fetch_failure_only_blocks_approval_recovery` even enshrines the write (`assert any("AI_STANDALONE_STALL_STATE_V1" in comment["body"] ...)`), locking the shadowing in as expected behavior.
  Why it fails at runtime: after any comments-GET outage (GET failing while POST still works — the exact asymmetry the new test simulates), previously budget-exhausted or mid-ladder standalone issues come back with a zeroed recovery count and a fresh clock, so the poller re-fires recovery actions (`/reclarify`, `/replan`, retrigger dispatches, judge runs) that `MAX_STALL_RECOVERIES_PER_ISSUE` had already stopped, burning Actions/LLM spend and spamming Telegram; repeated outages repeat the reset.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
